item.title: Senior Water Data Scientist | United States of America | Full time
item.description:
World Resources Institute, Mexico, United States of America

The Senior Water Data Scientist will serve as the technical and scientific lead for a flagship initiative focused on advancing how the impacts of nature-based solutions (NBS) and green-gray infrastructure (GGI) on water security outcomes are measured and monitored across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) and beyond. This role will help shape a next-generation approach to understanding causal inference and attribution for how NBS influence water availability, water quality, hydrologic regulation, drought resilience, flood risk, and watershed resilience, by convening partners to build the scientific methodologies and digital architecture that will make monitoring and measuring the water outcomes of NBS credible and accessible at scale.

The Senior Water Data Scientist will work with an interdisciplinary team across WRI’s Cities4Forests, Water Program, Global Nature Watch, Data Lab, and regional offices to identify, evaluate, and apply the best available science, data, models, artificial intelligence (AI) tools, and other emerging technologies for impact measurement and monitoring (IMM). The role will help bridge cutting-edge scientific research with practical implementation needs for utilities, investors, governments, and practitioners.

The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in one or more of the following areas:

  • planetary causal inference -> integrating planetary-scale data and localized information to derive insights about causality
  • AI, machine learning and data-driven environmental modeling -> Orchestrating research and scientific development with AI, such as expertise with geospatial foundation models (GFMs), experience with AI-assisted coding, and firm foundation in statistical and machine learning methods
  • remote sensing and Earth observation
  • geospatial analytics and environmental monitoring
  • environmental data systems and impact measurement frameworks
  • hydrology and watershed science
  • forest-water dynamics and ecosystem processes
  • integrated water resources management

The role requires a strong ability to synthesize emerging science and technology into actionable methodologies, frameworks, and recommendations that support investment-ready, scientifically credible approaches to monitoring water outcomes from NBS and GGI.

Scientific Leadership (50%)

  • Lead the technical development of research and analytical approaches related to measuring and monitoring the impacts of NBS and GGI on water security outcomes in LAC.
  • Lead and contribute to landscape syntheses, technical assessments, and methodological reviews related to hydrology, watershed monitoring, Earth observation, remote sensing, AI-enabled analytics, and environmental data systems.
  • Identify scientific, methodological, and data gaps that constrain credible measurement of water outcomes from NBS and GGI and help define pathways for future innovation and system-scale monitoring breakthroughs.
  • Evaluate the strengths, limitations, feasibility, and investment relevance of existing and emerging monitoring approaches, indicators, and data products.
  • Develop scientifically rigorous and policy-relevant recommendations for impact measurement and monitoring frameworks, indicators, methodologies, and monitoring strategies.
  • Possibility to manage other technical experts to deliver the project.

AI-Enabled Methods & Monitoring (20%)

  • Manage, analyze, and synthesize large and complex environmental datasets, including hydrologic, geospatial, remote sensing, climate, and ecological datasets.
  • Contribute technical expertise to the development of pilot monitoring approaches and applied field implementations with regional partners.
  • Support development and evaluation of advanced analytical approaches, including geospatial modeling, machine learning, AI-enabled workflows, and satellite-based monitoring systems where relevant.
  • Author and co-author high-quality knowledge products including reports, technical papers, synthesis documents, presentations, blogs, and peer-reviewed publications.
  • Help shape a long-term “technical vision” related to scalable water monitoring systems, foundational environmental datasets, and future “water cycle intelligence” approaches.

Project Development and Project Management (15%)

  • Co-lead the development and implementation of a multi-year initiative advancing water security impact measurement and monitoring for nature-based solutions and green-gray infrastructure.
  • Coordinate interdisciplinary collaboration across WRI teams and external partners, including research institutions, utilities, NGOs, technical advisors, and implementation partners.
  • Manage technical workstreams, project deliverables, timelines, peer review processes, and partner relationships to ensure high-quality project execution.
  • Co-lead the design and implementation of pilot projects and demonstration activities to test, validate, and refine monitoring approaches under real-world conditions.
  • Contribute to fundraising, proposal development, strategic partnerships, and donor engagement to expand WRI's water security and environmental data portfolio.

Stakeholder Engagement (15%)

  • Engage with technical experts, research institutions, NGOs, governments, utilities, companies, and other stakeholders (including those in Latin America and the Caribbean) to support knowledge exchange, collaboration, and applied learning.
  • Coordinate and contribute technical expertise to technical advisory group, including leading discussions, workshops, webinars, and external convenings.
  • Prepare presentations, briefings, and technical materials for internal and external audiences, including funders and senior decision-makers.
  • Help communicate complex scientific and technical concepts to non-technical audiences in clear, actionable, and decision-relevant ways.
  • Support coordination of project reporting, partner communications, and funder deliverables.

What will you need:

  • Education: A BA or BS degree (Graduate Degree preferred) in a relevant field: environmental science (such as hydrology, ecology, or water resource management), geographic science (such as remote sensing and satellite technology), or data science and programming (such as computer science, machine learning or artificial intelligence), or a related field required. Master’s Degree or PhD strongly preferred.
  • Experience: A minimum of 10 years of full-time work experience in environmental or climate science or a related field with rigorous quantitative and/or scientific components and a demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of interdisciplinary and multicultural teams. Experience working with Artificial Intelligence and data science is important. You have a proven ability to synthesize data analysis and research into policy-relevant written products.
  • Languages: Written and verbal proficiency in English, additional proficiency in Spanish is strongly preferred.
  • Requirements: Existing work authorization is required where this position is based. WRI is unable to authorize visa work authorization.

Potential Salary:

If based in the US: $139-175K

If located in another country office, salary will be determined by local market conditions.

Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors.

Please submit a resume with a cover letter by September 11, 2026. External applicants must apply through the WRI Careers portal to be considered. We may close for applications sooner if we receive a high volume of applications from qualified candidates.

item.title: Postdoctoral Scholarships at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution | United States of America | Full time
item.description:
Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Woods Hole, Massachusetts, United States of America

Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution is inviting applications for eighteen-month Postdoctoral Scholarships that are designed to extend the education and training of the applicants and to advance their research careers. Awards are granted to new and recent doctorates (within 3 years) in oceanography, chemistry, engineering, geology, geophysics, mathematics, meteorology, physics, biology, economics, marine policy, and any field that may contribute to WHOI’s core mission.

In 2027, Special Postdoctoral Scholarships will also be awarded in Marine Policy and Ocean Carbon Cycling. Additional awards may be available to support appointments in cross-cutting topics that are aligned with WHOI’s Campaign for Our Ocean that grow scholarly expertise in emerging areas of institutional strength. These areas may include Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, Coral Reefs, Defense-related Science and Technology, and Underwater Acoustics.

Criteria for awards include demonstrated research independence, productivity and novelty, and contributions to institutional research areas. Recipients will pursue their own research interests, mentored by resident staff. Applicants should identify and contact members of the Scientific and Senior Research Staff within one or more of our scientific departments, who share similar research ideas and are willing to serve as mentors.

Applications are due by October 15, 2026.

More information and application here: https://go.whoi.edu/pdscholarship

item.title: Assistant Professor, Tenure Track, in U-Pb Geochronology | Canada | Full time
item.description:
University of British Columbia, Vancouver, Canada

The Department of Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences (EOAS; www.eoas.ubc.ca) in the Faculty of Science at The University of British Columbia (UBC) seeks candidates for an Assistant Professor, Tenure Track, in U-Pb Geochronology, with an expected start date of July 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, and a salary within the range of $140,000-$150,000 per annum.

We seek an innovative geochronologist with expertise in developing and applying high-precision U-Pb petrochronological methods to fundamental questions in the solid Earth sciences. Candidates applying geochronological approaches to problems across the full breadth of hard-rock geology are welcome, including deep-time crustal evolution, tectonic tempos, igneous and metamorphic systems, ore deposit genesis, and planetary differentiation. The successful candidate is expected to leverage the department’s world-class analytical infrastructure and capitalize on existing departmental strengths in tectonics, orebody knowledge, geophysics, and geochemistry. We welcome and expect an openness to research collaboration within and beyond the department and UBC.

The successful candidate will have a Ph.D. in Earth Science or a related discipline at the time of appointment and will have made, or show promise of making, impactful petrochronological contributions to our understanding of the rates and timing of solid-Earth processes. Candidates should possess a strong record of research productivity commensurate with their experience and be able to communicate a clear research vision. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a robust, externally funded and internationally recognized research program, successfully supervise graduate students and postdoctoral fellows, and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in the Earth sciences. Although we recognize that candidates may have varying levels of teaching experience, a willingness to engage in active learning strategies and innovative teaching at the undergraduate level is expected. They will have a strong commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion, to create a welcoming community for all, particularly those who are historically, persistently, or systemically marginalized.

About EOAS and UBC

EOAS is Canada's largest and highest-ranked Earth Sciences department, ranked 13th globally in the latest QS World University Rankings. It offers a uniquely interdisciplinary environment with internationally recognized excellence in research, innovative teaching, and experiential learning spanning the full breadth of Earth, ocean, and atmospheric sciences. EOAS fosters a vibrant, collaborative community that brings together expertise in geology, geophysics, oceanography, atmospheric science, hydrogeology, geological engineering, and environmental science to advance understanding of the Earth system and address complex challenges related to natural resources, natural hazards, climate, and the environment.

UBC’s campuses are located on the traditional, ancestral and unceded territories of the Syilx (Okanagan) Peoples and of the Coast Salish Peoples, including the territories of the xwməθkwəy̓əm (Musqueam), Skwxwú7mesh (Squamish), and Stó:lō and Səl̓ílwətaʔ/Selilwitulh(Tsleil Waututh) Nations, and within one of the world’s great natural laboratories. Direct access to the North American Cordillera, including active volcanic arcs, deeply exhumed metamorphic complexes, Precambrian cratons, and world-class mineral districts, provides exceptional opportunities for field-based research and experiential learning. Vancouver is a global centre for mineral exploration, with a long history of collaboration between industry and UBC, particularly through the EOAS-hosted Mineral Deposit Research Unit (MDRU). Consistently ranked among the world's most livable cities, Vancouver also offers unparalleled access to mountains, the ocean, and a vibrant, culturally diverse urban environment.

Analytical Facilities

The successful candidate will be expected to leverage core analytical facilities hosted within EOAS in support of their research and teaching activities:

  • Pacific Centre for Isotopic and Geochemical Research (PCIGR): A flagship facility for isotope geochemistry and geochronology with an extensive suite of instrumentation and experienced technical leadership. Capabilities include single zircon dating via both laser ablation ICP-MS and chemical abrasion–thermal ionization mass spectrometry (CA-TIMS, equipped with a full suite of 1013 resistors); dedicated class-100 clean laboratories to enable ultra-low blank Pb work (<0.2 pg Pb blanks); and a recently installed triple-quadrupole ICP-MS (ICP-MS/MS).
  • Electron Microbeam and X-ray Diffraction Facility (EMXDF): A state-of-the-art facility for micro-analytical characterization of geological and materials samples, featuring scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with EDS capabilities, electron microprobe (EPMA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and cathodoluminescence imaging.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be expected to:

  • Develop and sustain an internationally recognized, externally funded research program in geochronology with strong integration of mineralogy and petrology;
  • Supervise and mentor graduate students and postdoctoral researchers;
  • Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in their area of expertise, as well as broader courses within the EOAS curriculum
  • Help sustain and continue to develop PCIGR, including its infrastructure and technical team;
  • Engage in departmental, university, and professional service activities;
  • Work collaboratively with EOAS faculty and research units (e.g. PCIGR, EMXDF and MDRU (Mineral Deposit Research Unit)), the broader UBC community, and with external partners, including industry, government, and Indigenous communities.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will have:

  • PhD in Earth Sciences or a closely related field, completed by the time of appointment;
  • Research focus including igneous and/or metamorphic processes;
  • Evidence of excellence in the field of U-Pb geochronology via, for example, method development, technical papers, conference contributions;
  • A strong record of research productivity commensurate with career stage, demonstrated by peer-reviewed publications;
  • Demonstrated ability to attract external research funding, or clear potential to do so;
  • Evidence of, or clear potential for, excellence in teaching and student supervision;
  • A strong commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion, to create a welcoming

community for all, particularly those who are historically, persistently or systemically

marginalized.

Preferred:

  • Hands-on experience with mass spectrometry and geochronological techniques;
  • Expertise in electron microbeam techniques (EPMA, SEM-EDS);
  • Postdoctoral research experience.

Applications must be submitted electronically via Academic Jobs Online using the following link: https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32504

They should upload a single PDF file that includes:

  • a cover letter;
  • a detailed curriculum vitae including list of publications;
  • a research statement (maximum 2 pages) describing current and future research directions, including how the candidate intends to use EOAS facilities;
  • a teaching statement (maximum 2 pages) outlining teaching philosophy and experience;
  • a diversity statement (1 page) describing your lived background experience (if comfortable), and your past experience and future plans regarding working with a diverse student body, and contributing to a culture of equity and inclusion;
  • the names and contact information for three referees.

The closing date for applications is October 14th, 2026. After the applications close, referees will be contacted for those applicants selected for further consideration, and may be asked to provide letters within a three-week time-frame. Initial interviews will be conducted in late-October 2026, with in-person interviews tentatively scheduled for January 2027.

Questions should be directed to the Search Committee at jobs@eoas.ubc.ca.

UBC hires on the basis of merit and is committed to employment equity. Equity and diversity are essential to academic excellence. An open and diverse community fosters the inclusion of voices that have been underrepresented or discouraged. Inclusion is built by individual and institutional responsibility through continuous engagement with diversity to inspire people, ideas, and actions for a better world. We encourage applications from members of groups that have been marginalized on any grounds enumerated under the B.C. Human Rights Code, including sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, racialization, disability, political belief, religion, marital or family status, age, and/or status as a First Nation, Métis, Inuk, or Indigenous person. UBC acknowledges that certain circumstances may cause career interruptions that legitimately affect an applicant’s record of research or educational leadership achievement. We encourage applicants to note in their applications whether they would like consideration given to the impact of any circumstances, such as those due to health or family reasons, in order to allow for a fair assessment of their research productivity.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be given priority, and members of historically marginalized groups will be given special consideration.

If you have any needs or questions regarding accommodations or accessibility during the job application, recruitment and hiring process or for more information and support, please visit UBC’s Center For Workplace Accessibility website at https://hr.ubc.ca/health-and-wellbeing/working-injury-illness-or-disability/centre-workplace-accessibility or contact the Centre at workplace.accessibility@ubc.ca.

The University is committed to creating and maintaining an accessible work environment for all members of its workforce. Within this hiring process we will make efforts to create an accessible process for all candidates (including but not limited to disabled people). Confidential accommodations are available on request by contacting Hazel Evangelista at email: hevangelista@eoas.ubc.ca

item.title: CSEi Research Fellow | United States of America | Full time
item.description:
University of Chicago - Climate Systems Engineering initiative (CSEi), Chicago, United States of America

Position Description

The Climate Systems Engineering initiative (CSEi) at the University of Chicago invites applications for the 2027-29 cohort of CSEi Research Fellows, to be appointed at the rank of Research Fellow. We seek outstanding early career scholars interested in any aspect of climate systems engineering.

The University of Chicago is building a substantial research cluster, including the anticipated addition of ten new faculty lines, on the science, technology, and public policy of Climate Systems Engineering. Our goal is to advance understanding of the benefits, risks, and governance of technologies that might reduce the impacts of accumulated greenhouse gases, and to educate students who will face the challenges of managing industrial civilization on a fragile planet. The CSEi’s topical scope includes open-system carbon removal such as enhanced rock weathering, solar geoengineering, and interventions to limit the loss of glacial ice. The CSEi welcomes research from across fields including the sciences, humanities, social sciences, public policy, and law.

The CSEi Research Fellows program aims to develop the next generation of research leaders who will shape the future of climate systems engineering for the benefit of people and the planet. CSEi Research Fellows will work closely with UChicago faculty mentors, but their research and funding are independent. The program will help them develop strong research networks by facilitating collaboration among the Research Fellows cohort and by ensuring that they have ample opportunities to interact with the whole community of CSEi-affiliated faculty and research leaders. Securing a faculty mentor in advance is strongly preferred, and applicants are encouraged to reach out early to engage a mentor. UChicago faculty members from any discipline may potentially serve as mentors, regardless of whether they have prior experience with climate systems engineering.

To offer a sense of the range of opportunities for collaboration, leading faculty from a variety of fields have contributed statements about research interests and possibilities for collaboration. These statements, available on the CSEi website, are examples of how faculty research interests might overlap with climate systems engineering. Applicants may reach out to any UChicago faculty member about these or other topics.

This is a two-year position, starting between August 3 – September 16, 2027, that offers a $95K salary per year, dedicated workspace, and research and travel funding of $10,000 per year.

This position is benefits eligible - for information on benefits, please consult the University of Chicago Benefits Guide: https://mybenefits.nfp.com/UChicago/benefits-guide/.

Additionally, the University will provide a one-time payment of $4,000 for relocation assistance, payable at the end of the first month of employment at the University. Please note that this payment is taxable.

Teaching is not required, though an optional teaching opportunity during the second year of the fellowship may be available, subject to need and requisite approval. In-person interaction is a crucial part of the program, and Research Fellows are expected to participate actively in the life of the CSEi.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Completion of all requirements for a Ph.D. or other terminal degree appropriate to the field is required at the time of appointment.

Preferred:

  • 0-3 years professional experience.
  • Pre-matching with a faculty mentor and enthusiastic recommendation from the mentor.
  • Academic and professional success in the early career stage (typically graduate school and the first three years after completion of degree) and the potential to make an important contribution to the field of climate systems engineering.

Residency

The fellowship requires residency in the Chicago area.

Application Instructions

Applications must be submitted online via Interfolio at: https://apply.interfolio.com/191139

The following materials are required:

  • C.V.
  • Statement of research objectives that explains how the research will advance understanding of climate systems engineering, and how the research relates to the applicant’s prior work and skills. (maximum 2 pages).
  • Writing sample consisting of a chapter, essay, or article.
  • Two letters of reference: please provide contact information for two letter writers.
  • Name of UChicago faculty member who has agreed to serve as mentor. If applying without a pre-matched mentor, please provide the names of faculty members whom you want to work with and an explanation of why you were not able to secure a mentor in advance.

Complete applications must be submitted via Interfolio by 11:59 PM Eastern Time on November 2, 2026.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

The University of Chicago is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, national or ethnic origin, shared ancestry, age, status as an individual with a disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, or other protected classes under the law. For additional information please see the University's Notice of Nondiscrimination.

Job seekers in need of a reasonable accommodation to complete the application process should call 773-834-3988 or email equalopportunity@uchicago.edu with their request

item.title: PhD Position on Root-Soil interactions | Denmark | Full time
item.description:
Aarhus University, Aarhus, Denmark

The PhD student is expected to join the project ComPASS - Compaction-driven mechanisms of Plant Adaptations and Signalling: the role of ethylene in root responses.

The overarching objective of the project is to provide a fundamental understanding of how physical processes occurring in the vicinity of root tips influence root growth via ethylene signalling. The project entails laboratory experiments during which plants/genotypes of different ethylene sensitivity will be grown under controlled conditions on different soils. The soils will be chosen in order to cover a range of textures and bulk densities (compaction treatments). After the growth period, pots will be scanned with X-ray CT to characterize root traits and root-soil physical interactions (root-soil contact, rhizosphere structure) non-destructively in 3D. RNA sequencing will be performed on root tip tissues in order to identify expressed genes and signalling pathways that are affected as a response of changes in soil properties. This project is a collaboration between Aarhus University, the Helmholtz Center for Environmental Research in Halle (Germany) and the University of Nottingham (UK). Place of employment is in the Department of Agroecology of AU. The PhD student will be expected to participate in research stays in at least one of these two collaborating institutions.

Please apply via the AU portal at this link:

https://phd.tech.au.dk/for-applicants/apply-here/saeropslag/compass-compaction-driven-mechanisms-of-plant-adaptations-and-signalling-the-role-of-ethylene-in-root-responses

item.title: PhD position on Mixing in turbidity currents in experiments and submarine canyons (4yrs) | Netherlands | Full time
item.description:
Utrecht University, Faculty of Geosciences, Department of Earth Sciences, Utrecht, Netherlands

The Department of Earth Sciences is looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate with an MSc background in Earth Sciences, Civil or Hydraulic Engineering, or other appropriate fields. You will work on the project: DEEP-FLUX: Journey of low-density particles to the DEEP ocean floor – terrestrial organic carbon and microplastics FLUX through submarine canyons.

Your job

More than 10,000 submarine canyons connect the continents to the deep ocean. These canyons are the conduits for transport of land-derived materials to the ocean floor in avalanche-like events called turbidity currents. Turbidity currents transport enormous amounts of sediment and Particulate Organic Carbon (POC) and bury this in deposits below the ocean floor. They additionally convey abundant nutrients and oxygenated water masses, which together with the POC (as food) support conditions for abundant life at unexpected depths in the absence of light for photosynthesis. Submarine canyons are also called the ‘human connection to the deep sea (Dissanayaka et al., 2023)’. Unfortunately, this connection brings land-derived pollutants (microplastics, pesticides, pharmaceuticals) into the very heart of these ecodiverse hotspots, making them vulnerable to far-field human interference. While this general knowledge is now firmly established, the processes of transport and burial during turbidity current events remain poorly understood.

The DEEP-FLUX project aims to establish a new physical framework for quantifying fluxes of POC and microplastics from land to the ocean floor. The project team will eventually consist of 4 PhD candidates and the PI (Joris Eggenhuisen). Together they will:

  1. perform scaled-down laboratory experiments that will reveal the physical mechanisms of transport and burial of microplastics and POC in turbidity currents down submarine canyons;
  2. incorporate these mechanisms into an existing computer model for sediment flux through submarine canyons; and
  3. validate the model on monitored submarine canyons.

The responsibility of the PhD position advertised here will mainly involve experiments on mixing in turbidity currents, and experimental tests of turbulent diffusion characteristics of microplastics and POC.

Training

A personalised training programme will be set up reflecting your training needs and career objectives. About 20% of your time will be dedicated to this training component, which includes following courses and/or workshops (some of which are mandatory), as well as training on the job in assisting in the bachelor’s and master’s degrees programmes of the department at Utrecht University.

Your qualities

We seek candidates who are motivated by the proposed research, take initiative to develop ideas, are self-driven, and can work both independently and within a team. Applicants should hold an MSc degree in Earth Sciences, Physical Geography, Oceanography, Civil or Hydraulic Engineering, or a related discipline by the time the position starts. Furthermore, you should have:

Experience in experiments with water and/or sediment

  • Coding experience
  • A willingness to contribute to team goals
  • A flair for written, graphical, and oral communication
  • And above all, creativity and curiosity

Due to the international character of our research, good command of spoken and written English is essential. We highly encourage applicants from all members of our community and of diverse backgrounds to join us.

Terms of employment

We offer:

  • a position (1.0 FTE) for 1 year, with an extension to a total of four years upon a successful assessment in the first year, and with the specific intent that it results in a doctorate within this period;
  • a working week of 36 - 40 hours and a gross monthly salary between € 3.204 and €4.051 in the case of full-time employment (salary scale P under the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO NU));
  • 8% holiday pay and 8.3% year-end bonus;
  • a pension scheme, partially paid parental leave and flexible terms of employment based on the CAO NU.

In addition to the terms of employment laid down in the CAO NU, Utrecht University also offers a range of its own schemes for employees. This includes arrangements for professional development, various types of leave, and options for sports and cultural activities. You can also tailor your employment conditions through our Terms of Employment Options Model. In this way, we encourage you to keep investing in your personal and professional development. For more information, please visit Working at Utrecht University.

For informal information (not for application) about this position, please contact Dr Joris Eggenhuisen at j.t.eggenhuisen@uu.nl.

To apply, please use this link to go to the advertisement on our own website and follow the guidelines mentioned there.

Include the following information in your application:

  • your curriculum vitae, including any courses taken that are relevant for the position;
  • a letter of motivation, which will be evaluated on the following themes:
    • Motivation to pursue a Doctorate degree
    • Motivation to apply for this specific project
    • Fulfilment of the qualifications outlined in this vacancy

No reference letters need to be submitted in your initial application. If you are short-listed, we will contact you for referees. We aim for a quick selection procedure after the application deadline of October 2nd, 2026. The position is available from January 1st, 2027.

Note that international candidates that need a visa/work permit for the Netherlands require at least four months processing time after selection and acceptance. This will be arranged with help of the International Service Desk (ISD) of our university. Finding appropriate housing in or near Utrecht is your own responsibility, but the ISD may be able to advise you therewith. In case of general questions about working and living in The Netherlands, please consult the Dutch Mobility Portal.

Knowledge security screening can be part of the selection procedures of academic staff. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. Online screening may also be part of the selection. Commercial response to this ad is not appreciated.

item.title: Lab Manager in the Environmental Geochemistry Laboratory | Germany | Full time
item.description:
University of Freiburg, Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany

Description

The newly established laboratory of the Group of Applied Geochemistry is seeking a motivated person with a technical or scientific background to join our team and share our enthusiasm for experimental environmental geochemistry and interdisciplinary research.

Our group investigates fundamental and applied questions in environmental geochemistry, with a focus on contaminant behavior, groundwater protection, and biogeochemical element cycling. We study the interactions of inorganic contaminants and nutrients with minerals and their role in environmental processes. Combining biogeochemical, mineralogical, and hydrogeochemical approaches with state-of-the-art analytical methods, we aim to advance our understanding of geochemical processes and develop innovative strategies for the sustainable protection of natural resources.

Your tasks

As a laboratory manager, you will play a key role in establishing, developing, and ensuring the smooth operation of the Applied Geochemistry Laboratory. A central analytical instrument in our laboratory is a new LC-ICP-MS, which enables the quantification of elemental species at trace concentrations. The laboratory infrastructure also includes an IC, AAS, UV/VIS, XRD, TOC, SEM, and a Mössbauer spectrometer. Your responsibilities will also include:

  • You will oversee laboratory maintenance, procurement, and safety management.
  • You will train and support staff and students in using laboratory infrastructure and conducting experiments.
  • You will develop technical solutions and optimize analytical methods, particularly for ICP-MS applications, together with doctoral researchers and postdocs.
  • You will support research projects through laboratory work, field activities, sampling, and measurements.
  • You will assist with field and laboratory practical courses.

Your profile

You enjoy working in an international environment and are excited to take on a wide range of tasks. With a hands-on attitude, you seek out solutions and have a keen sense for efficiently organizing laboratory processes. You are motivated to help shape a new laboratory and tackle both routine and more complex challenges. You also bring:

  • At least a bachelor's or university degree (FH) in environmental sciences, geosciences, chemistry or a related field, or a comparable professional qualification.
  • Solid theoretical and practical expertise in water or environmental analysis.
  • Openness to and enthusiasm for innovative technologies, with a willingness to learn new topics.
  • A good understanding of technical and environmental chemistry.
  • A careful, reliable, and precise working style.
  • Good knowledge of German and English (at least B2 level in both languages).
  • Strong teamwork skills and intercultural competence.

Our offer

You can look forward to an exciting and diverse role within an inspiring team that fosters creativity and values open, respectful communication. Additionally, we offer you:

  • The chance to actively shape the development of our laboratory.
  • Flexible, family-friendly working hours.
  • The opportunity to work independently and on your own responsibility while being part of a team.
  • A supportive and collaborative work environment that fosters both personal and professional growth.
  • Bright and modern office and laboratory spaces in a centrally located, historic building within walking distance of the train station.
  • Job ticket, further training and company pension scheme (VBL).

Please submit your application as a single PDF file via the University’s application portal at https://uni-freiburg.de/en/job/00005140/ to Prof. Kerstin Hockmann, including the following documents:

  • A cover letter describing your motivation for the position and your earliest possible starting date.
  • Your CV and an overview of your analytical experience
  • Certificates, and relevant qualifications
  • Contact information for professional references or reference letter from previous employers

For further information, please contact Prof. Kerstin Hockmann on the phone number +49 761 6464 or E-Mail info@geochem.uni-freiburg.de.

The position is unlimited. The salary will be determined in accordance with E11 TV-L.

item.title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Environmental Geochemistry | Germany | Contract
item.description:
University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany

The Applied Geochemistry group at the Institute of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Albert-Ludwigs-University of Freiburg, Germany, is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral reseacher in environmental geochemistry.

The research group, led by Prof. Kerstin Hockmann, integrates applied and environmental geochemistry to investigate element cycling in soils, sediments, and surface waters. Using an interdisciplinary approach, we study (bio)geochemical processes involving key elements such as iron, carbon, and sulfur, and their impacts on trace element mobility and mineral properties in environments affected by human activities and climate change.

Your role and impact:

  • Initiate and conduct scientific research projects, including acquiring funds.
  • Apply and develop novel analytical approaches to investigate (bio)geochemical processes in both field and laboratory settings.
  • Supervise and mentor students in the laboratory in close collaboration with our lab manager.
  • Teach in the B.Sc. and M.Sc. programs at the Institute of Earth and Environmental Sciences, including laboratory courses and field excursions.

The role provides an excellent opportunity to strengthen your independent research profile within a dynamic and growing research team, with the freedom to pursue your own research ideas and the support needed to secure follow-up funding. You will have the opportunity to present your research at international conferences, contribute to the supervision of PhD, M.Sc., and B.Sc. students, and benefit from tailored mentoring to advance your scientific career.

Your profile:

The candidate must hold a qualified PhD in (bio)geochemistry, environmental chemistry, geo-microbiology, organic geochemistry, or a related field, and has an intellectual curiosity about the many interdisciplinary aspects of environmental geochemistry. Our laboratory is equipped with state-of-the-art analytical instrumentation for water and environmental analyses, including expertise in synchrotron-based spectroscopy. A strong interest in developing and applying analytical methods, as well as in interdisciplinary collaboration, is required. Proficiency in written and spoken English is essential, with German considered an asset.

item.title: PhD Project: Sulfur Cycling in Wetlands and its Coupling to Iron and Carbon | Germany | Contract
item.description:
University of Freiburg, Germany

The Applied Geochemistry group is offering a PhD position at the Institute of Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Freiburg (Germany). Our group studies element cycling in soils, sediments, and surface waters using an interdisciplinary approach, with a focus on environments affected by human activities and climate change.

Project background

Sulfur cycling is a fascinating but still surprisingly understudied part of wetland biogeochemistry. In oxygen-limited environments such as peatlands, the Wadden Sea, and other wetlands, sulfate can be rapidly transformed into sulfide. Sulfide, in turn, reacts strongly with iron minerals and can promote the dissolution of Fe(III) oxides, setting off a cascade of reactions that influence both iron and carbon cycling.

Despite its importance, many aspects of sulfur cycling in terrestrial wetlands remain poorly understood. One reason is that sulfur compounds are unstable, making them difficult to capture with conventional analytical methods.

This PhD project will investigate sulfur redox transformations in wetlands and their links to iron and carbon cycling. The project combines experimental work with analytical method development to characterize different sulfur species using techniques such as HPLC and LC-ICP-MS. The project also offers the opportunity for fieldwork in the Black Forest, where the PhD candidate will investigate sulfur pools and transformations in minerotrophic peatlands.

Tasks and Responsibilities

  • Design and conduct laboratory experiments
  • Apply and develop analytical methods for sulfur speciation
  • Acquire and analyze synchrotron-based research data
  • Identify suitable field sites in the Black Forest and establish contact with landowners and relevant authorities
  • Publish research results in peer-reviewed journals and present them at conferences
  • Contribute to teaching and supervise laboratory practical courses

Requirements

  • A degree (MSc or equivalent) in environmental science, geoecology, environmental chemistry, geomicrobiology, or a related field
  • Strong motivation for interdisciplinary research
  • A collaborative mindset, scientific curiosity, and willingness to travel for field campaigns and networking events
  • Strong interest in environmental geochemistry and analytical method development
  • Excellent command of written and spoken English; knowledge of German is an advantage
  • A driver’s license (B) is beneficial

We offer

  • An engaging and supportive working environment that fosters scientific curiosity, creativity, and interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Access to state-of-the-art research facilities in our newly equipped laboratory
  • Opportunities to attend and present your research at national and international conferences
  • Close scientific supervision and comprehensive onboarding into the research group

Applications should be submitted through the University of Freiburg job portal on https://uni-freiburg.de/en/job/00005154/ and should include a CV, a motivation letter, copies of relevant degree certificates and contact information for two references.

Applications will be reviewed starting early October 2026, and the position will remain open until filled. The ideal start date is November 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter. Employment follows University of Freiburg regulations (TV-L A13, 70%). The position is limited to 3 years.
